conclusion.kind: static code-path inference, not a new wire observation
conclusion.expected_connection_lifetime: One lazy MemoryBook per actual stdio transport lifespan on the event-loop thread, for an existing stable on-disk database.

inheritance_chain: Product serve calls FastMCP.run(transport=stdio); its stdio branch invokes anyio.run(run_stdio_async).
FastMCP lifespan_wrapper enters the product lifespan in the same task. Product lifespan creates _BookResource(owner_thread=get_ident()) and sets its own ContextVar before yielding.
Low-level Server.run enters that lifespan before creating the ServerSession and starting each _handle_message through an AnyIO task group.

AnyIO asyncio TaskGroup._spawn calls loop.create_task without overriding context. Python Task copies the current Context when none is passed. The copied Context holds the same mutable _BookResource object; it does not clone the Book.
SDK request_ctx.set changes a separate request ContextVar; it does not reset the product resource ContextVar.

FastMCP.call_tool awaits ToolManager.call_tool, which awaits Tool.run, which awaits FuncMetadata.call_fn_with_arg_validation. For synchronous functions its branch directly returns fn(**arguments_parsed_dict), with no to_thread/run_sync/executor boundary.
Product acquire_book therefore observes the active resource and same owner thread under the normal path. A stable before/after (st_dev,st_ino) retains the Book until transport cleanup.
intentional_temporary_connection_cases: Direct SDK calls without transport lifespan
Inactive resource retained by a stale context
A foreign thread, including copied ContextVars under asyncio.to_thread
Missing/unusable file identity or a newly created file without stable before/after identity
Database replacement: close old Book and retain a new one only after stable identity checks
memo_cleanup: MemoryBook initializes _token_count_memo=None, lazily creates it for the first token-budget recall, and attaches the same memo to each ordinary TokenCounter on that Book.
MemoryBook.close clears retained memo entries/encoder identities in a finally block, including exceptional close cleanup; counters remain cumulative.
TokenCounter.count/_ExactTokenMemo.lookup invalidate a memo when certified encoder/core identity changes or eligible encoding loses certification. Ordinary fixed encoders preserve the memo.

The external DELETE FROM recall_cache in the frozen MCP helper changes query-result records only; there is no corresponding _token_count_memo clear/reset path. Each MCP configuration intentionally gets a new server process, so warmth is not shared across configurations.

test_coverage.manual_lifespan_real_sdk_calls: test_lifespan_reuses_one_connection_and_preserves_payload_and_schema counts one open across four gathered direct server.call_tool calls and one close at lifespan exit, with schema/payload equality.
test_coverage.fallback_guards: Direct/no-lifespan and asyncio.to_thread calls assert temporary connection closure; exceptional lifespan cleanup, distinct servers, file replacement and unusable inode cases are covered.
test_coverage.actual_stdio: test_real_stdio_observes_external_writer_and_invalidates_cached_recall uses ClientSession/stdio and checks repeated results and external ingestion visibility, but does not count Book/SQLite constructors or closes.
test_coverage.token_stdio: test_stdio_strict_integer_and_compact_detailed_budget_parity checks real protocol argument types and exact budgets, not Book or token-memo reuse.
test_coverage.gap: No existing real-stdio test records the connection count/thread/memo identity. Successful wire payload equality alone cannot distinguish retained connections from correct per-call fallback.

next_observation: No additional calls planned here. That observation remains diagnostic, not a new formal timing sample.

normal_result_cache_static_review.baseline_boundary: Actual MCP uses default cache_size=128/use_cache=True and retains the normal read/write transaction path; native formal calls use cache_size=0/use_cache=False. This legitimate surface difference must remain.
required_work: Recheck revision under the write lock
Serialize and INSERT OR REPLACE the complete native result only when revision still matches
Prune by original touched_ns ordering and configured capacity
normal_result_cache_static_review.low_risk_small_candidate: A private reusable stdlib JSONEncoder with the exact existing ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True and compact separators can avoid constructing that encoder on every _json call; actual gain is unmeasured and likely small. Preserve ordinary stdlib encoding, output bytes, errors and per-call local encode state; do not introduce cached response strings.
normal_result_cache_static_review.not_prioritized: A touched_ns pruning index can help a populated production result cache but adds index write/storage costs and requires tie-order scrutiny. It offers no evident leverage when a normal query leaves a single row, so it is not a justified primary C6 direction without SQL evidence.
not_equivalent_without_more_proof: Skipping writes/pruning based on benchmark cache clearing
Moving result serialization before the guarded revision check (extra work/error behavior on concurrent changes)
Replacing the guarded revision SELECT with INSERT SELECT while unconditionally serializing its parameters
Changing result-cache payload, touched time, eviction semantics or SQLite durability
normal_result_cache_static_review.recommendation: Keep every real MCP cache write and choose larger work reduction from the planned SQL-template/reuse trace. No unconditional safe large reduction in the normal cache write path is established by static reading.
